title: Resolvent algebras and limit states of interacting canonical ensembles
abstract: The limit states of canonical ensembles of a large number of interacting bosons at a given temperature, which are confined by harmonic forces, are studied in the framework of the resolvent algebra. It is shown that the limits satisfy the KMS condition or are ground states, regardless of the type of interaction. In case of attractive forces, where the ensembles collapse, observables that become meaningless in the limit disappear from the limit representations. For repulsive forces, this can also happen if condensates with an infinite number of particles in the same state (proper condensates) appear in the limit. The resulting structures and their interpretation are illustrated by a simple model. The study of vanishing harmonic forces (thermodynamic limit) involves changes of the dynamics. It is conveniently based on derivations acting on the algebra. They are given by the commutator of the Hamiltonians with the elements of the algebra. To ensure that the images remain in the algebra, the interaction must be regularized. This is accomplished in a manner that has only a minor impact on the dynamics and may be of broader interest. With this input a relation between the strength of the confining harmonic forces and the number of particles in the ensembles is derived from the condition that the limit states are to be stationary (invariant) under the adjoint action of the unconfined, spatially homogeneous limit dynamics. This relation encompasses the conditions that are frequently used in studies of Bose-Einstein condensates.
summary: This paper develops a rigorous mathematical framework using resolvent algebras to study the thermodynamic limit of interacting bosonic ensembles. It proves that the limiting states must satisfy fundamental physical criteria like the KMS condition or be ground states. This provides deep theoretical insight into how equilibrium properties emerge in large, interacting quantum systems.
main_problem: The study focuses on determining the limit states of canonical ensembles for interacting bosons as particle number or confinement length approaches infinity.
main_result: The limit states are shown to satisfy either the KMS condition or be ground states, providing a rigorous framework for analyzing thermodynamic limits in bosonic systems.
method: The analysis employs resolvent algebras and C*-dynamical systems theory to study time evolution via automorphisms and weak-star convergence of Gibbs ensembles.
model_or_system: The system models interacting bosons confined by harmonic forces, described on Fock space. The Hamiltonian is analyzed in the limit where confinement length $L 	o \infty$ (thermodynamic limit).
key_observables: KMS condition states, ground states, and observables that survive the limiting process.
important_parameters: Temperature ($ eta$), particle number ($n$), and confining force strength/length ($L$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the existence of suitable regularizations for operators to maintain mathematical structure in the limit.
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the resolvent algebra and dynamics ($\mathcal{A}_{\alpha L}$), establishing convergence theorems for the thermodynamic limit ($L 	o \infty$), and deriving relations between confining forces and particle numbers based on stationarity conditions.
why_interesting: This work provides advanced mathematical tools (resolvent algebras, C*-dynamics) to rigorously handle phase transitions and equilibrium states in interacting quantum many-body systems, which is crucial for understanding Bose-Einstein condensates and other strongly correlated regimes.
